analysis.title: US Economic Weekly: Midterm mal(AI)se
key_insights: BofA argues that more AI and data-center regulation after the midterms may slow the AI capex boom only marginally. A bust would depend on demand and monetization, and for now demand indicators support aggressive capex plans.

Since the election, the S&P 500 is down 2.8%, the Nasdaq is down 5.5% and the semiconductor index is down 14%. This extends declines seen from Sep 1 to election day (S&P -1.2%, Nasdaq 100 -3.7%, semis -8.5%).

Democrats won gubernatorial races in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, which together hold 35% of data center capacity under construction by power and 38% of planned capacity. 40 of 41 data-center-opposing ballot measures passed and 76% of voters oppose a data center in their community.

BofA expects state and local data-center restrictions to pick up next year, mainly policies that insulate consumers from higher utility costs and stronger environmental standards. It does not expect these to affect the roughly 70GW of data center power now under construction.

BofA's equity strategy team estimates AI-related revenue growth will start to exceed AI capex growth as early as 3Q 2027, which can justify about 350GW of planned or under-construction data center capacity. BofA still expects AI investment to add 30-50bp to growth next year.

BofA sees only modest scope for tariff relief. The deficit is $2tn and tariffs raised about $310bn in the last 12 months (nearly 1% of GDP). Likely beneficiaries are traditional allies (EU, Canada, Mexico, Japan, Korea), which account for about a third of tariff revenue.

Oct CPI is due Tuesday 11/10. BofA forecasts headline and core CPI at +0.2% m/m against consensus of +0.3% headline and +0.2% core. The BLS will not publish a y/y figure because October 2025 data were not collected during the shutdown.
BofA initializes its Oct core PCE estimate at 0.2% m/m (0.22% unrounded, 3.2% y/y) and says this keeps a December hike firmly on the table.
3Q GDP tracking rose 0.4pp to 3.8% q/q saar after construction spending, durable goods, factory orders and trade balance data. The advance 3Q GDP print was 3.4%.

BofA expects the Fed to hike 25bp in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027, reaching a terminal rate of 4.25-4.50% held through end-2027. The Fed held in October. Risks are two-sided: falling behind the curve, or stopping after one hike if y/y core PCE rolls off on base effects.

BofA forecasts 2026 growth of 2.6% 4Q/4Q and 2.1% in 2027. Core PCE should finish 2026 slightly above 3% and fall to 2.5% in 2027. Job growth should average 70k/mo in 2026 and about 60k in 2027-28, with the unemployment rate at 4.1% through 2027.

Fed speakers lean hawkish. Logan said at least two more 25bp hikes are needed and Musalem said more firming will be necessary soon. Barkin and Hammack favored gradual or smaller, more frequent adjustments, and Bowman saw no urgency in October.
Weekly BofA card data show total card spending per household +6.2% y/y in the week ending Oct 31, with gas +25.0%, furniture -4.1% and department stores -8.1%.
Oct data this week: ISM manufacturing 55.5 vs 54.5 consensus, ISM services 54.5 vs 54.8, JOLTS 7523k vs 7164k, ADP 86k vs 67k. The Oct payrolls report was listed as not released in the document.

BofA's rate forecasts put the 10-year Treasury at 5.00% by Dec 2026 (spot 4.83%) and the 2-year at 5.00% (spot 4.46%). It forecasts EUR-USD at 1.15 and USD-JPY at 152 by Dec 2026 (spot 1.12 and 157.71).

sector_views.rationale: BofA expects regulation to act as a speed bump rather than stop the capex cycle, with demand and hyperscaler capex plans for 2027 revised higher again.
Citing Ross Fowler, election results in Florida, Louisiana, North Dakota and Oklahoma are positive for the sector, and tighter rules in Texas, Georgia or Ohio could shift projects to other states.

earnings_insights: Hyperscaler AI-related revenue growth continues to climb (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, ORCL, as of 11/5/2026), per BofA US Equity & Quant Strategy.
Per BofA strategists, hyperscalers were penalized for any softness in results, while 2027 capex expectations were revised higher again.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA expects a softer print than the prior two months, driven by lower energy prices.
In line with consensus. BLS will not publish a y/y figure.
BofA says this keeps a December hike firmly on the table.
Due Friday 11/13. Core PPI is forecast at 0.3% m/m.
Up 0.4pp on the week. The advance estimate was 3.4%.
Starting point for BofA's tracking estimate.
BofA forecasts hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027, then a hold through end-2027.
Underlying inflation is stuck above target, with risks skewed to the upside.
Growth supported by AI capex and a resilient consumer.

risk_factors: State and local data-center regulation could delay the point where AI revenue growth outpaces capex growth.
Monetization of AI and possible cannibalization of existing revenue streams could end the capex cycle.
The Fed could fall behind the curve by hiking slowly and end up hiking more.
Inflation risks are skewed to the upside because of tariffs, energy prices and the Iran war.
A deficit of $2tn limits room to cut tariffs.

geopolitical: Tariffs and the Iran war are cited as sources of the current inflation overshoot.
Midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep, with possible effects on tariff policy and AI and data-center regulation.
Tariff relief, if any, would most likely go to the EU, Canada, Mexico, Japan and Korea.

tension_points.bull_case: Regulation is a speed bump. About 70GW of power is already under construction, hyperscaler 2027 capex plans were revised higher, and AI revenue growth is expected to exceed capex growth by 3Q 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Voter opposition to data centers has risen, and Democratic wins in TX, OH and GA, which hold 35% of capacity under construction, raise the risk of stricter rules and higher costs. Monetization concerns are already hurting hyperscaler stocks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI-related revenue growth failing to outpace capex growth, or demand growth no longer outpacing supply growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Hikes at a quarterly pace in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027 are enough because growth is solid and the labor market is balanced.
tension_points.bear_case: Moving slowly could leave the Fed behind the curve, forcing more hikes later.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Y/y core PCE rolling off on favorable base effects early next year would let the Fed stop after one more hike in Dec 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: Regulation will slow the AI investment boom only marginally, and demand drives whether it busts.
theme_stances.evidence: Increased regulation seems more likely after the midterms.

theme_stances.theme: Fed hikes in Dec and Mar
theme_stances.key_argument: Growth is solid, inflation is too high and policy has been too easy, so two more hikes are expected at a quarterly pace.
theme_stances.evidence: we still expect two more hikes

theme_stances.key_argument: A $2tn deficit means the government cannot afford to lose much tariff revenue.
theme_stances.evidence: We see only modest scope for tariff relief.
